chapter: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
title: Leaving Detroit for New York in 1937
summary: After a 'female problem' he moves on, stops in Cleveland, and arrives to see stars outside 2040 Seventh Avenue.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So what made you go to New York? In '37...was it '37?

Yeah, whenever I have a female problem (laughter), I always move on. Like Jimmy Shine, I will pack my clothes and move on down the line (laughter). I had a problem in Detroit, female problem, So I decided to come to New York, you know, to move to New York. And usually when I made those decisions was at night. And as a rule, in most instances, I left in the morning. I make overnight decisions, you know, I make a snap decision.

And I left New York and I went to Cleveland. Stopped by to see Art and Lanny Scott, and then from there I came on to New York. When I got to New York, it was something else. I used to walk out in front of 2040 Seventh Avenue and I'd see Louis Armstrong and Cab Calloway and Cootie Williams and Sonny Greer and Ivie Anderson and Mary Lou Williams, you know, all coming to New York to play the Apollo Theatre... coming to New York to make recordings, or coming to New York... passing through, and you just never knew who you'd see next. You just never knew. And it was a thrill each time. I don't mean an emotional...I mean, not an outburst, but within,

there was this thrill of am I glad this guy lied, this trumpet player that was trying to teach me lied, and the thrill to know that the woman asked me, you know, to help her do that housework. A thrill to think about Ella B. Moore. But most of all it was a thrill that my mother let me do these things, you know...that she allowed me to pursue my own career and charter my own course, and I don't think when she looked back that she can say that I didn't try to...and the final analysis was always good you see.
